title: Ember and Choir Again
premise: When the border wards of Thornfell shatter and the stars go dark, exiled storm-caller Vesper Fairweather discovers her family's old debt: her sister's soul was sold to the court beneath the mountain to buy the wards' power. Hunted by the usurper's armies and guided by a disgraced court musician who once loved her sister, Vesper descends through smuggler roads into the Undercourt to steal the soul back before the solstice binding makes the sale permanent. The price of survival demands a soul in exchange, and Vesper must choose between her sister and the free cities that exiled her. In the end she splits the storm inside herself, paying half her own soul to free her sister and rekindle the stars, earning a battered, partial homecoming.
about_author: Mara Villalobos is a former cartographer who spent a decade mapping mountain passes across three continents before turning to fiction. She writes fantasy about borders, debts, and the people who live in the gaps between them.

chapters.title: The Night the Stars Went Out
chapters.summary: Vesper's POV. Smuggling salt and secrets through Thornfell, Vesper feels the border wards die as a cold snap kills the stars overhead. She shelters a wounded courier carrying a sealed writ bearing her family name. The emotional beat is dread sharpening into recognition: her exile's peace is over, and the writ names her sister.

chapters.title: A Debt Written in Salt
chapters.summary: Vesper's POV. The writ reveals the Fairweather bargain: her sister Wren's soul sold to the Undercourt to fuel the wards, payment due at solstice. Vesper seeks her old fence, Bramble, who warns the usurper's armies are already marching. Emotional beat: guilt, as Vesper realizes her exile left Wren to pay the family price alone.

chapters.title: The Singer in the Cellar
chapters.summary: Vesper's POV. Tracking Wren's trail, Vesper finds Ilex, a disgraced Undercourt musician hiding in a smuggler's cellar, who once loved Wren and knows the court's roads. He offers passage in exchange for escape from his own debts. Emotional beat: wary alliance; Vesper distrusts anyone who loved her sister and stayed behind.

chapters.title: Armies on the High Road
chapters.summary: Ilex's POV. Fleeing ahead of the usurper's vanguard, the pair witnesses a burned free-town and Ilex reveals the usurper's goal: the Undercourt's throne, and the souls banked beneath it, including Wren's. Emotional beat: horror and resolve; survival now means descent, not flight, as Vesper chooses the mountain over the sea.

chapters.title: Doors That Remember Names
chapters.summary: Vesper's POV. Using smuggler roads and her storm-calling blood, Vesper opens a sealed Fairweather door into the mountain's roots. The door demands a memory as toll, and she surrenders her mother's lullaby. Emotional beat: grief as currency; Vesper begins learning what inheritance truly costs.

chapters.title: The Court Beneath
chapters.summary: Ilex's POV. The Undercourt in all its terrible beauty: masked nobles, soul-lanterns, and a regent who greets Ilex by name. They learn Wren's soul is the solstice binding's keystone, and that the usurper's emissaries are already bargaining. Emotional beat: seduction and menace; the court offers Vesper her old life back if she abandons Wren.

chapters.title: What the Lanterns Keep
chapters.summary: Vesper's POV. In the soul-vault, Vesper finds Wren's lantern and speaks to the fragment of her sister inside, learning Wren chose the sale to protect Vesper from the family debt. Emotional beat: shattering love; Vesper's mission transforms from rescue into repayment, and she vows no more Fairweather sacrifices.

chapters.title: The Usurper's Bargain
chapters.summary: Ilex's POV. The usurper's armies breach the mountain's crown; the regent offers Vesper a trap: kill Wren's binding and the wards stay dead, dooming the free cities. Ilex betrays his own escape route to buy Vesper time, nearly dying. Emotional beat: sacrifice compounding; duty and love now point in opposite directions with armies closing in.

chapters.title: Solstice, Storm-Called
chapters.summary: Vesper's POV. At the binding, Vesper calls every storm she has ever hoarded, splits her own soul in half, and pays it to unmake Wren's sale and reignite the star-wards. The court's lanterns blaze back to life as light returns overhead. Emotional beat: climax and transfiguration; Vesper survives the price, but only half of her walks out.

chapters.title: Half a Soul, Whole a Home
chapters.summary: Shared POV. Vesper and Wren, both diminished and both free, climb out of the mountain into starlight as the free cities rally. Ilex stays below to rebuild the court's music; Vesper chooses to stay in Thornfell rather than return to her old exile. Emotional beat: bittersweet resolution; inheritance remade as choice, love outlasting duty's price.
